evidence: Draft judged: “If you can’t do this in a loving way today, just put your hands there and see what you feel. Don’t fake it.” Compared word for word with the words it replaces (“…see what you feel. You don’t have to fake it!”), the first sentence is identical, so the only real change is the last sentence: the permission formula with an exclamation mark becomes a plain three-word instruction. That matches the_change (Emulate's two sentences, last sentence as ci and cg have it) and the draft appears once in CONTEXT.txt, as the end of the single paragraph under “Inner child love”, directly after “Make sure you are actually talking to your inner child, who is scared to death.” MEANING against his published fallback (“No warmth today? Then rest your hands there and notice what you find, no faking required.”): no warmth today (“can’t do this in a loving way today”), rest the hands there (“just put your hands there”), notice what you find (“see what you feel”), no faking (“Don’t fake it”) are all present, in his order, and nothing is added. The one shift is force: “no faking required” and “You don’t have to fake it” permit, while “Don’t fake it” instructs. I weighed it: the same published passage tells the reader “Don’t recite the words like an incantation you’re hoping the subconscious will grade” and this paragraph already says “Make sure you are actually talking to your inner child”, so a plain “don't” about authenticity is the register of this passage; the act asked for is identical (do not perform warmth); and the permission to do less survives in the unchanged first sentence (“just put your hands there”). READ IN CONTEXT: I read the whole section first. No seam: “this” is saying the words lovingly, “there” is the heart and solar plexus, both named before, so C02 is clean; the apostrophes are curly like the script's; I saw no Emulate artifact (no space before the full stop, “can’t” and “Don’t” correct, no stray quote marks); the blunt voice sits with “scared to death” and “Make sure you are actually…”. The change also removes a real problem: “You don’t have to fake it!” repeated the script's own “You don’t have to fix it.” a few lines up (T26 and the T10 formula, plus the exclamation), and the draft has neither. TELL ROWS: T01, T03 to T08, T11, T12, T16, T18, T19, T23 to T25, T27 ABSENT (no first person stake, scene, prop, filler, image-plus-explanation, bridge, matched pair, contrast, announcement, scenery, faux insight, colon reveal or tic word). T02 ABSENT (two sentences, one step and one rule). T10 ABSENT (the formula went with the replaced sentence; the fallback is local to this practice and comes from his guide). T21 ABSENT (one short job per sentence). T22 ABSENT (a step and a rule from his guide, not reassurance alone). T26 ABSENT (“in a loving way” appears twice in the paragraph, but the second is a deliberate callback, “this” pointing back to the first, and it is in the unchanged first sentence). T09 and T13 (the D9 pointers) ABSENT: only the last sentence changed, and the paragraph's own noticing (“who is scared to death”) is in the unchanged text. T14, T15 ABSENT (nothing moved; no thesaurus swap; the first sentence is unchanged from the words it replaces and the last is plainer). T17 ABSENT (an instruction, not a thesis or aphorism). T20 and T29 are the closest rows and the lint's B7 flag, so I tested them. The paragraph does end on this line (the writer's reason that the stop lines go on after “quiet” belongs to another section and does not apply here; I rely on the other half of the reason). It is a plain instruction with no figure, antithesis or twist, a short sentence is not a tell by itself, the slot was already a short closer in the replaced words (and the worse one), and this section has one paragraph, so no run of short landings. T29 test: without it the paragraph still makes sense, but the sentence carries his protected no-faking point and says what not to do with the hands-only fallback, which the first sentence only implies, so it is not a restatement for its own sake. T28 ABSENT (a rule, not uplift or a lesson). C01, C03, C04 ABSENT. LINT FINDINGS: B7 accepted for the reasons just given. D9 accepted: a splice of the same passage's points in order by construction, and T13 and T09 are not happening. E36/E41 accepted: the linter's 13.0 per 100 is 3 second-person words (“you”, “your”, “you”) in 23; the words it replaces have 4, so the change lowers it, and the paragraph is direct address to the reader throughout. No unjustified tell, no added claim, meaning kept.
